source.section: Schedule M line 47 Senior Citizen Deduction columns (a)-(d) (PDF p.6; instructions PDF p.29; example PDF p.30; PDF p.23 'Taxpayers over age 65 or disabled'; Tax Division page: 'You receive the higher of the $8,000 modification or the sum of various itemized decreasing modifications'); Schedule M line 32 Military Retirement Modification (PDF p.5; instructions PDF p.28; PDF p.22 'Certain State and Federal Retirement Systems'); IT-140 lines 1-8 (PDF p.3; instructions PDF p.26: exemptions 2,000 each, line 7 floored at zero); Rate Schedules I and II (PDF p.37); Tax Table (PDF p.38 on)

worked: Married filing jointly, both 65 or older: your military retirement 20,000 uses up your own 8,000, but not your spouse's; each person's line 47 is figured in that person's own column. You (Column A) born 1958-10-10, age 67 at December 31, 2025; Spouse (Column B) born 1959-12-12, age 66 at December 31, 2025. Federal AGI (given) = private pension 10,000.00 (you) + military retirement 20,000.00 (you) + IRA distribution 30,000.00 (spouse) = 60,000.00. Federal taxable income (given, not tested) = 60,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 - 2 x 1,600.00 aged 65 or older = 25,300.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). IT-140 line 1 federal AGI 60,000.00. Schedule M additions lines 51-58 none; IT-140 line 2 0.00. Schedule M You (Column A): line 32 military retirement 20,000.00 (in full, no cap); line 47 (age 67): column (c) income not on lines 35-46 = 30,000.00, limited to 8,000.00: 8,000.00; column (d) lines 29-34 = 20,000.00; line 47 = 8,000.00 - 20,000.00, less than zero, so 0.00; line 49 = 20,000.00. Schedule M Spouse (Column B): line 47 (age 66): column (c) income not on lines 35-46 = 30,000.00, limited to 8,000.00: 8,000.00; column (d) lines 29-34 = 0.00; line 47 = 8,000.00 - 0.00 = 8,000.00; line 49 = 8,000.00. Line 50 total subtractions = 20,000.00 + 8,000.00 = 28,000.00. Projection (per person): You (Column A): Social Security subtraction 0.00; age 65 deduction = lesser of (8,000.00 - military retirement 20,000.00) and own income 30,000.00 = 0.00; best_of_group wv_line_47 keeps the larger, 0.00 (wv_social_security); Spouse (Column B): Social Security subtraction 0.00; age 65 deduction = lesser of (8,000.00 - military retirement 0.00) and own income 30,000.00 = 8,000.00; best_of_group wv_line_47 keeps the larger, 8,000.00 (wv_senior_citizen_deduction). Projection subtractions total 28,000.00, the same as line 50. IT-140 line 3 subtractions 28,000.00; line 4 West Virginia AGI = 60,000.00 + 0.00 - 28,000.00 = 32,000.00. Line 5 Low-Income Earned Income Exclusion: federal AGI over 10,000, none. Line 6 exemptions 2 x 2,000.00 = 4,000.00. Line 7 taxable income = 32,000.00 - 4,000.00 = 28,000.00. Line 8 tax by Rate Schedule I (PDF p.37) bands: 2.22% x 10,000.00 = 222 + 2.96% x 15,000.00 = 444 + 3.33% x 3,000.00 = 99.9; total 765.9 = 765.90. The Tax Table row 28,000 to under 28,060 (PDF p.38 on) gives 767; expected keeps the schedule formula on the exact income. No Family Tax Credit (Modified Federal AGI above the table limits); credits 0.00; state income tax 765.90.
accepted_approximations: Tax below 100,000 of taxable income is figured on the exact income, where the booklet uses a Tax Table row's midpoint rounded to the whole dollar. Other tax is also rounded to the whole dollar in the booklet.
